name: Nuclear / Uranium
tagline: A commodity-driven boom-bust theme riding the nuclear revival and AI-datacenter power demand. Returns hinge on the uranium spot price and are dominated by a few miners — above all Cameco — plus real single-country (Kazakhstan/Canada) risk.
universe_note: Spans pure uranium miners (URNM, URNJ), miner-heavy (URA), and diversified nuclear-power baskets (NLR utilities-tilt, NUKZ reactors+utilities+fuel). The broader funds (NLR/NUKZ) are far less Cameco/uranium-spot dependent. XLE is the broad-energy benchmark. Use 'Add ticker' for others (URNU etc.).
key_tensions: Uranium spot-price dependence: these funds live and die on the uranium price — a volatile commodity with a brutal boom-bust history (URNM: +40.6% in 2025 but -14.1% in 2024).
Cameco concentration: one company dominates — ~23% of URA and ~21% of URNM. A single miner's operational or production news moves the whole fund.
Single-country / geopolitical risk: uranium supply is concentrated in Kazakhstan (Kazatomprom) and Canada (Cameco) — production cuts, export policy, or geopolitics there hit the whole theme.

Miners vs physical vs utilities: URNM holds some PHYSICAL uranium (purest spot-price proxy); URA/URNJ are miner equities (leveraged to the price); NLR tilts to nuclear UTILITIES (Constellation, PSEG) — steadier but a different bet.
Junior miners are far riskier: URNJ holds mid/small/micro-cap miners (top-10 ~79%!) — maximum leverage to uranium prices and maximum drawdown risk.
Why XLE is the yardstick: a narrow single-commodity bet vs broad, cash-generative energy. XLE (oil & gas, 0.08%) shows what you give up in diversification and what you take on in volatility.
benchmark_note: XLE (broad energy) is the yardstick, NOT a nuclear fund — it's oil & gas majors (Exxon, Chevron). It shows the contrast: a narrow, high-volatility single-commodity uranium bet vs cheap (0.08%), diversified, dividend-paying energy. Use it to judge whether the uranium concentration was rewarded.
